cases.sentence: ___, оказывается, почти всегда идёт куда бы то ни было.
cases.translation: The road, it turns out, almost always goes somewhere, no matter where.
cases.explain: «Дорога» is the subject of the verb «идёт» (to go), so it takes the nominative case.

cases.sentence: ...чтобы благонравное дитя предавалось губительной праздности, которая есть мать всех ___.
cases.translation: ...which, as is known, is the mother of all vices.
cases.explain: Genitive plural «пороков» expresses possession/type after «мать всех» (mother of all vices).

cases.sentence: ...что по ___ природы его и не полагается.
cases.translation: ...that according to the laws of nature it isn't even supposed to exist.
cases.explain: The preposition «по» governs the dative case: «по законам» = 'according to the laws.'

cases.sentence: Вот вы, например, ___ от старых привычек хотите отучить.
cases.translation: You, for example, want to wean a person off old habits.
cases.explain: «Человека» is the direct object of the verb «отучить» (to wean someone off), requiring the accusative case.

cases.translation: ...benefits guaranteed by the arguments of reason and arithmetic.
cases.explain: Instrumental plural «доводами» shows the means by which the benefits are 'guaranteed' (гарантированных чем).

cases.sentence: У них есть одно удивительное здание в этом же ___, навеки нерешимое – муравейник.
cases.translation: They have one remarkable building of this same kind, permanently unresolved — the anthill.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» governs the prepositional case here: «в этом же роде» = 'of this same kind.'

reading.ru: Господа, я, конечно, шучу, я сам знаю, что неудачно шучу, но ведь нельзя же все принимать за шутку.
reading.question: What does the narrator admit at the start of Chapter 9?
options: That he is joking, and not very well
That he has never joked before
reading.correct: That he is joking, and not very well
reading.explain: He says he is joking, and admits he jokes 'unsuccessfully.'

reading.ru: Вот вы, например, человека от старых привычек хотите отучить и волей его исправить, сообразно с требованиями науки и здравого смысла.
reading.question: What does the narrator accuse "you" (his imagined opponents) of wanting to do?
options: Wean a person off old habits and correct his will according to science and common sense
Teach a person new habits through punishment
reading.correct: Wean a person off old habits and correct his will according to science and common sense
reading.explain: He says 'you want to wean a person off his old habits and reform his will, in accordance with science and common sense.'

reading.ru: Одним словом, почему вы знаете, что такое исправление действительно принесет человеку выгоду?
reading.question: What question does the narrator raise about "correction" (improvement)?
options: Whether such correction will actually bring a person benefit
Whether correction is popular among scientists
reading.correct: Whether such correction will actually bring a person benefit
reading.explain: He asks how they know that such correction will really bring a person benefit.

reading.ru: Я согласен, человек есть животное, но преимущество созидающее, принужденное стремиться к цели сознательно и заниматься инженерным искусством, то есть вечно и беспрерывно дорогу себе прокладывать, хотя куда бы то ни было.
reading.question: What does the narrator concede that man is, despite calling him an animal?
options: A creature that constructively strives toward a goal and builds roads, wherever they may lead
reading.correct: A creature that constructively strives toward a goal and builds roads, wherever they may lead
reading.explain: He agrees man is an animal, but a 'creative' one compelled to consciously strive toward a goal and engineer roads.

reading.ru: Человек любит созидать и дороги прокладывать, это бесспорно.
reading.question: What does the narrator say is "indisputable" about man?
options: That he loves to build and lay roads
That he loves to destroy everything
reading.correct: That he loves to build and lay roads
reading.explain: He states plainly, 'Man loves to create and build roads, that is indisputable.'

reading.ru: Не потому ли, может быть, он так любит разрушение и хаос, ведь это бесспорно, что он иногда очень любит это уж так, что сам инстинктивно боится достигнуть цели и довершить созидаемое здание.
reading.question: Why does the narrator suggest man might love destruction and chaos?
options: Because he instinctively fears reaching the goal and completing the building he is creating
Because chaos is required by science
reading.correct: Because he instinctively fears reaching the goal and completing the building he is creating
reading.explain: He speculates man instinctively fears achieving the goal and finishing the edifice he is building.

reading.ru: У них есть одно удивительное здание в этом же роде, навеки нерешимое – муравейник.
reading.question: What remarkable, permanently settled structure do ants have, according to the narrator?
reading.correct: The anthill
reading.explain: He says the ants have a remarkable, eternally settled building of this kind — the anthill.

reading.ru: Но человек – существо легкомысленное и неблаговидное, и, может быть, подобно шахматному игроку, любит только муравейников.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe man, in contrast to the ants?
options: A frivolous and unseemly creature, perhaps like a chess player, who only loves anthill-building
A wise and dignified creature who values stability
An insect indistinguishable from an ant
reading.correct: A frivolous and unseemly creature, perhaps like a chess player, who only loves anthill-building
reading.explain: He calls man 'a frivolous and unseemly creature' who, like a chess player, only loves the anthill-building process.

reading.ru: Может быть, что вся та цель на Земле, к которой человечество стремится, только заключается в одной этой беспрерывности процесса достижения цели.
reading.question: What does the narrator speculate humanity's entire earthly goal might actually consist of?
options: The uninterrupted process of striving toward the goal itself, not the goal
reading.correct: The uninterrupted process of striving toward the goal itself, not the goal
reading.explain: He says the whole goal humanity strives for may consist solely in the continuity of the process of achieving it.

reading.ru: А ведь дважды 24 есть уже не жизнь, господа, а начало смерти.
reading.question: What does the narrator claim "twice two is four" (the formula) actually represents?
options: The beginning of death, not life
reading.correct: The beginning of death, not life
reading.explain: He says 'twice two is four is no longer life, gentlemen, but the beginning of death.'

reading.ru: Достижение он любит, а достигнуть уже не совсем, и это, конечно, ужасно смешно.
reading.question: What is "terribly funny" about man, according to the narrator?
options: He loves the process of achieving but not quite achieving the goal itself
reading.correct: He loves the process of achieving but not quite achieving the goal itself
reading.explain: He says man loves achievement itself but not quite the achieving, calling this terribly funny.

reading.ru: Ведь, может быть, человек любит не одно благоденствие, может быть, он ровно настолько же любит страдания, может быть, страдания-то ему ровно настолько же и выгодны, как благоденствие, а человек иногда ужасно любит страдания, да страсти.
reading.question: What does the narrator suggest man loves just as much as well-being (prosperity)?
reading.correct: Suffering
reading.explain: He suggests man loves suffering exactly as much as he loves well-being.

reading.ru: Стою я за свой каприз, не за то, чтобы он был мне гарантирован, когда понадобится.
reading.question: What does the narrator say he stands up for?
reading.correct: His own caprice (whim)
reading.explain: He declares, 'I stand up for my own caprice,' not for it being guaranteed to him.

reading.ru: А между тем, я уверен, что человек от настоящего страдания, то есть от разрушения и хаоса, никогда не откажется.
reading.question: What is the narrator convinced man will never renounce?
options: Real suffering, that is, destruction and chaos
reading.correct: Real suffering, that is, destruction and chaos
reading.explain: He is certain man will never give up real suffering — destruction and chaos.

reading.ru: Сознание, например, бесконечно выше, чем дважды два.
reading.question: What does the narrator claim is "infinitely higher" than twice-two?
reading.correct: Consciousness
reading.explain: He states that consciousness, for instance, is infinitely higher than twice two.

reading.ru: Вы верите в хрустальное здание, навеки нерушимое, то есть в такое, которому нельзя будет ни языка украткой выставить, ни кукиша в кармане показать.
reading.question: What do "you" (the audience) believe in, at the start of Chapter 10?
options: An eternally indestructible crystal building at which one could never stick out one's tongue or make a rude gesture
A wooden hut that can be destroyed
reading.correct: An eternally indestructible crystal building at which one could never stick out one's tongue or make a rude gesture
reading.explain: He says 'you' believe in a crystal edifice, eternally indestructible, at which one could never even secretly stick out a tongue.

reading.ru: «Если вместо дворца будет курятник и пойдет дождь, я, может быть, и влезу в курятник, чтобы не замочиться, но все-таки курятника не приму за дворец из благодарности, что он меня от дождя сохранил.
reading.question: If it rains and only a henhouse is available instead of a palace, what does the narrator say he will do, yet still refuse to do?
options: He'll climb into the henhouse to stay dry, but still refuse to call it a palace out of gratitude
He'll refuse to enter the henhouse at all
He'll declare the henhouse better than any palace
reading.correct: He'll climb into the henhouse to stay dry, but still refuse to call it a palace out of gratitude
reading.explain: He says he might climb into the henhouse to avoid getting wet, but still won't mistake it for a palace out of gratitude.

reading.ru: Это моё хотение, это желание моё.
reading.question: How does the narrator describe his insistence on living "in mansions" rather than settling for mere shelter?
options: It is his own wanting, his own desire
It is a law of nature
reading.correct: It is his own wanting, his own desire
reading.explain: He says plainly, 'This is my wanting, this is my desire.'

reading.ru: У меня есть подполье.
reading.question: What does the narrator say he has, defending his refusal to compromise?
reading.correct: The underground (his "подполье")
reading.explain: He declares simply, 'I have the underground.'

reading.ru: Зачем же я устроен с такими желаниями?
reading.question: What question does the narrator ask about why he was made the way he is?
options: Why he was made with such desires
Why he was made to be joyful
reading.correct: Why he was made with such desires
reading.explain: He asks, 'Why am I made with such desires?'

reading.ru: Он хоть и способен молча в подполе 40 лет просидеть, но в школе выйдет на свет, да прорвется, так уж говорит, говорит, говорит.
reading.question: What does the narrator predict about the "underground man" once he emerges into the light?
options: Though capable of sitting silently underground for 40 years, once out in the light he will burst out talking endlessly
He will immediately become a scientist
He will forget everything he thought
reading.correct: Though capable of sitting silently underground for 40 years, once out in the light he will burst out talking endlessly
reading.explain: He says our underground brother, though able to sit silent underground for 40 years, will burst out talking, talking, talking once in the light.
